transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I can’t seem to shut my brain off anymore. It starts with something small, like a client not responding to an email, and then within minutes I’m thinking I’m going to lose the contract, fall behind on divorce payments, and never get back into a real leadership role. It just keeps going, and I can’t stop it.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of your life, not just work?

Yes. It’s not just work. My mind jumps around a lot — from contract stuff to mortgage payments, to whether people in the Bethesda tech circles think I’m damaged goods. Even something like a recruiter taking too long to email me back can feel like proof that my whole career is closing down.
Do you ever get sudden rushes of intense fear or physical panic that peak within minutes?
I’m not really sure I’d call it that. I don’t think I get these sudden attacks that peak in a few minutes. It’s more like the worry builds and stays there, if that makes sense.
When the worrying starts, do you feel able to control or stop it?

No, not really. Once it starts, I have a very hard time stopping it. It’ll begin with one thing, like a client not answering, and then my mind just runs with it — losing the contract, money problems, not getting back into a leadership role. I know it sounds like a chain reaction, but in the moment I can’t seem to shut it down.
Has this kind of hard-to-control worry been happening on most days for at least 6 months?
Yes. It’s been going on pretty much since I was fired, which was about thirteen months ago. I thought it might ease up once I found contract work, but it really hasn’t let up.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized or wired and needed much less sleep than usual?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve had plenty of times where I couldn’t sleep well, but not because I felt energized or wired. I can’t think of a period like that.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I’m not sure I’d call it depressed. I’ve been down at times, yeah, but it feels more like being worn out and discouraged than, you know, a deep depression.
Do these thoughts feel intrusive and unwanted, like they pop into your mind even when you don’t want them to?

Yes, they do feel unwanted. It’s like my brain grabs onto one thing—say a client doesn’t respond—and then it just runs with it. Within minutes I’m thinking I’m going to lose the contract, fall behind on payments, and never get back into a real leadership job. I don’t want to think that way, but I can’t seem to shut it off.
When these thoughts hit, do you do anything over and over to try to neutralize them or feel reassured?

I don’t think I do anything like a ritual, if that’s what you mean. I might reread a message or check my email again, or ask myself if I missed something, but it’s more me trying to figure it out than doing some repeated thing to make the thought go away.
Do you feel this worrying is mainly a reaction to losing your job?

It started around losing the job, yeah, but it doesn’t stay there. My mind keeps jumping from contract work to the mortgage, to whether people in the Bethesda tech circles think I’m damaged goods. Even something like a recruiter taking too long to email back can feel like proof that my whole career is closing down.
Have you been feeling sad most of the day nearly every day?
I don’t know that I’d call it sad most of the day, nearly every day. I mean, I get down about all of this, but I’m not sure it’s that constant. It feels more like worry than sadness.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not sure. I still do things if I make myself, but I don’t know if I’m enjoying them the same way. It’s hard to tell because my mind is usually somewhere else.
Do you often feel physically restless or keyed up?

Yeah. I feel wound up most of the day, like I’m bracing for something bad to happen. My shoulders stay tight, and I’ll catch myself pacing around the house or bouncing my leg during calls, even when nothing is actually going on.
Do you often feel easily fatigued?
I’m not sure. I do get tired, but I haven’t really been tracking whether it’s more than usual or happening all the time. It’s hard for me to separate being tired from just feeling worn down mentally.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
I’m not really sure. I notice my mind wanders sometimes, but I can’t tell if it’s a concentration problem or just me being preoccupied. I’d have to think about it more.
Have you been feeling hopeless?
I don’t know that I’d call it hopeless. I get discouraged sometimes, but I’m not sure it’s that exactly.
If you had not lost your job, do you think this level of worrying would still be happening?

Honestly, yes. The job loss makes it worse, but I don’t think it’s only that. My mind keeps jumping from one thing to the next—contract work, the mortgage, whether people in the Bethesda tech scene see me as damaged goods. Even something like a recruiter taking too long to email me back starts feeling like proof my whole career is shutting down.
Has this worrying been interfering with your ability to function day to day?

Yes, it has. I’ve missed some networking follow-ups because I get stuck thinking through everything that could go wrong. And I’ve delayed client deliverables the same way—just overthinking and not moving.

I’ve also pulled back from soccer and seeing friends. I’m embarrassed by how tense and irritable I’ve been, so I just avoid people more than I used to.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes. Most nights I’m lying there replaying how I answered interview questions or thinking about what I should’ve said. I’ll wake up and check the clock at 2 or 3 in the morning, and then I’m just… stuck awake.

Even when I technically get enough hours, I don’t feel rested. It feels like I was on call all night for some system outage.
Before you lost your job, were you already someone who worried excessively about different areas of life?

Yes. I mean, the job loss gave it a clear target, but I was already like this. My mind would jump between work contracts, mortgage payments, and how people in the Bethesda tech circles were seeing me. Even something simple, like a recruiter taking too long to email back, could turn into me thinking my whole career was closing down.
